meta.blog-salderingsregeling.html.title: Net-metering scheme ends in 2027: what it means for your hotel · Lemnion
meta.blog-salderingsregeling.html.descri: From 1 January 2027 the net-metering scheme for solar panels ends. What does this mean for hotels? Self-consumption, batteries and smart charging determine your return.
blog-saldering.h1: Salderingsregeling stopt in 2027: wat dit voor jouw hotel betekent
blog-saldering.sub: From 1 January 2027 you can no longer offset your own solar power against your consumption. For hotels, making smart use of your own power therefore becomes more important than ever.
blog-saldering.intro: The net-metering scheme (salderingsregeling) ends on 1 January 2027. Anyone with solar panels can then no longer offset generated power against their own consumption. For hotels that is an important turning point: the value of your solar power shifts from feeding back to using it yourself. In this article we explain what changes and how you can make the best of it.
blog-saldering.kort-li1: The net-metering scheme ends on 1 January 2027: you can no longer offset power you generate against your consumption
blog-saldering.kort-li2: You can still feed power back, but until 2030 it yields at least 50% of the net supply rate
blog-saldering.kort-li3: Self-generated and directly used power remains fully free of tax and network charges
blog-saldering.kort-li4: For hotels, self-consumption becomes the key to a good return on solar panels
blog-saldering.kort-li5: A battery and smart charging help you use the surplus yourself
blog-saldering.p-wat: With net-metering you may offset the power you generate yourself against your own consumption. If you produce more in summer than you use, you can use that surplus in winter without paying tax on it. That way all your solar power was charged at the same rate as grid power. If your hotel feeds back 2,500 kWh, for example, you may use 2,500 kWh without electricity, network or energy-tax costs.
blog-saldering.p-verandert: From 1 January 2027 you may no longer offset the power you generate. You can still feed power back, but you receive compensation for it instead of it being offset against your consumption. A few things at a glance:
blog-saldering.verandert-li1: Until 2030 the feed-in compensation must be at least 50% of the net supply rate (the electricity rate excluding taxes)
blog-saldering.verandert-li2: Suppliers may charge feed-in costs for processing the power; the ACM supervises this
blog-saldering.verandert-li3: Power you generate and use directly remains free of tax and network charges and yields the highest saving
blog-saldering.h2-hotellerie: What does this mean for the hotel sector?
blog-saldering.p-hotellerie: How hard this shift affects you depends on the size of your connection. Smaller hotels that fall under small consumption can still net-meter now; for them the change is greatest. Larger hotels with a large-consumption connection already worked with a feed-in tariff and in fact already benefit from self-consumption. For all hotels it applies: the same solar panel only really pays off from 2027 if the power generated is also used on site.
blog-saldering.p-keuz: A kWh used yourself is worth several times more after 2027 than one fed back. Direct use saves the electricity price, the energy tax and the network charges. And the peak of your own generation falls exactly in the hours a hotel consumes most: kitchen, laundry, cooling and guests present during the day.
blog-saldering.p-zone: If you produce more during the day than you use directly, a battery stores the surplus for the evening and night. That way you shift your own cheap solar power to the moments you need it, instead of feeding it back at a low compensation.
blog-saldering.p-laden: Charge points and smart control can charge the electric cars of guests and staff exactly when your panels produce most. That makes charging infrastructure a natural consumer of your own solar power and keeps feed-in low.
blog-saldering.reken-h: 💡 Why a kWh used yourself is worth more
blog-saldering.reken-p: A kWh fed back yields at least roughly €0.10 to €0.13 from 2027 (50% of the net rate). A kWh used yourself saves the full supply rate plus taxes and network charges, roughly €0.25 to €0.35. Self-consumption is therefore two to three times as valuable as feeding back.
blog-saldering.actie-li1: Map your consumption: where and when your hotel uses power determines how much you can use yourself
blog-saldering.actie-li2: Maximise self-consumption: shift large consumers (kitchen, laundry, charging) to the peak of the sun
blog-saldering.actie-li3: Consider a battery: store the midday surplus for the evening peak
blog-saldering.actie-li4: Connect charge points smartly: charge electric cars during daylight and use your own solar power
blog-saldering.bron: Source: rijksoverheid.nl, page on the net-metering scheme (checked September 2026).
